text:
emma.k: Heads up — PR #482 adds a 'prefetch bootstrap' section to the Optimize toolkit but I realized we didn't call out behavior for short-sequence workloads (short prompt + streaming).

sam.w: Thanks, will review. Do you mean how KV cache warm-up interacts with batching when seq_len < 16?

emma.k: Exactly. In our internal benchmarks we saw 2x latency on the first stream token for batch_size=1 because the prefetch path triggers a cold load. We should recommend an explicit kv_prefetch: "warm" flag for short sequences and show a snippet.

tyler.r: Could we also add a note on quant profiles? When we switch to int4 the cold-load penalty is bigger because kernel selection path differs.

joan.s: Agree. Proposal: small table + code sample showing: default config, +kv_prefetch warm, +reduced batch_timeout for streaming. Keep it short.

emma.k: Draft snippet (please sanity-check):
```yaml
optimize: 
  kv_prefetch: warm   # pre-populate prefix KV cache for short sequences
  batch_policy:
    max_batch: 8
    batch_timeout_ms: 10  # lower for streams
  quant_profile: auto:int8
```

sam.w: That snippet looks fine. Suggest we add an inline explanation: when to prefer int8 vs int4 for short prompts (int8 recommended for first-token latency).

tyler.r: Also add a short code note for SDK users showing the client-side hint: `client.request({prefetch: true})` so folks using the JS/Go SDKs can mirror the behavior.

emma.k: Good call. I'll add a 1-line JS example.

sam.w: Minor doc nit: link ARM/AMP kernel caveat to our runtime page (https://redwood.ai/docs/runtime-kernels). Otherwise lgtm.

joan.s: I'll take ownership of the PR checklist: add a test case to examples/shortseq that runs a 5-token streaming sample and asserts tail latency < 30ms after warm prefetch.

docbot: CI passed for 482 (linux-build, docs-lint).

emma.k: Thanks — I'll push the edits in the next hour. Can someone review before EOD?

tyler.r: I can review after standup.

sam.w: Same.

emma.k: Quick follow-up: should we include a fallback note recommending - if prefetch isn't available - to use a small dedicated batch pool instead of disabling prefetch? That avoids cold-loads for low-QPS services.

joan.s: Yes, add it under 'Operational recommendations' as one bullet.

emma.k: Perfect, updating now.

sam.w: Awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:
